clue.text: Avoiding it, guest means to save face

indicators.note: avoiding here means steering clear of, so the two letters of the next word are left out of the guest

parts.note: a guest is a visitor
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on how a guest might keep their dignity by sidestepping something awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IT from VISITOR to leave the answer. 'Save face' looks like the idiom for keeping dignity, but a visor literally protects the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a shield worn to protect the face, such as on a helmet.

clue.text: Clamour involved farce about one in ballot

indicators.note: in says the rearranged farce, with its letter for one, goes inside the word for ballot

parts.note: a ballot is a vote

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters of farce surround the numeral for one
involved means twisted and complicated, so the letters of farce are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A protest over a ridiculous episode involving one person in an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges farce to CFERA, and 'about' wraps that round I to make CIFERA, which goes 'in' the ballot word. The election surface hides the clamour definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To vociferate is to shout loudly and insistently, to cry out noisily.

clue.text: Kind of jump, finally taking off

definitions.text: Kind of jump, finally taking off

indicators.note: finally taking off says the final letter is removed from the word for jump

parts.note: to skip is to jump lightly

explanation.surface: A description of a type of leap at the moment of launch.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIP loses its last letter. The whole clue also describes the winter sport's jump, where you finally take off from the ramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski jump is a ramp event in which competitors on long runners launch into the air.

clue.text: One may remove characters pencilled in for a set of games

definitions.text: One may remove characters pencilled in
definitions.meaning: an eraser, which wipes away letters written in pencil
a series of matches in bridge or tennis, decided by the best of three

explanation.surface: Something that erases pencil writing, or a series of contests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is just a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain an eraser goes by this name, and a deciding series of games is also called one.

clue.text: Bloody awful sport — strictly for the birds!

definitions.text: Bloody awful sport — strictly for the birds!

parts.words: Bloody awful sport — strictly for the birds!
parts.note: 'for the birds' usually means worthless, but here it is literal: a blood sport contested only by roosters

explanation.surface: A disgusted verdict on some brutal pastime as worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: This banned blood sport pits gamecocks against each other, so it is literally fought by birds.

clue.text: Given coverage, MP's trapped, having to admitted suppression

indicators.note: trapped means the politician is caught inside the word for given coverage

parts.note: clad means clothed or covered
MP stands for Member of Parliament, a UK politician
to own, or own up, is to admit

explanation.surface: A news report of an MP caught out and forced to accept a crackdown.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'having to admitted', apparently a slip for 'having to admit', since own up means admit, not admitted. 'Having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is a firm crackdown, an official effort to suppress some activity.

clue.text: Predictably, some raised a drink …

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters run upwards, so they are read backwards
some means only part of the next word is used, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Some people, as expected, lifted their glasses for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside PREDICTABLY is REDIC; 'raised' turns it upwards in this down clue. The ellipsis leads on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apple juice.

clue.text: …since nobody's up in the morning

parts.note: for can mean since or because

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: nobody is no one; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: An explanation, following on from the last clue, that nobody is awake yet in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns NO ONE upwards to give ENOON in this down clue. 'In' is a link word, and the ellipsis carries on from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The forenoon is the part of the day before midday, an old word for the hours after dawn.

clue.text: Give information on feeding system for this chirpy creature

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing to the police
a hopper is a funnel-shaped container that feeds material into a machine

explanation.surface: An instruction to tell people about how this lively animal is fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' here is British criminal slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: This leaping insect makes a chirping sound by rubbing its legs against its wings.

clue.text: Some weighty reading coming my way

definitions.meaning: headed towards me, as two words

explanation.surface: A heavy book being passed in my direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a big scholarly volume; split in two the letters also mean directed at me.

clue.text: Part of film directors viewed as support for script?

parts.note: a clip is a short excerpt from a film
a company's directors together form its board

explanation.surface: Film-making talk: a slice of the movie that the directors see as backing the script.
explanation.walkthrough: The film-world surface makes 'directors' look like movie directors; they are company directors, the board. 'Viewed as' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipboard is a stiff writing backing that holds sheets of paper, so it physically supports written script.

clue.text: Indisputable male domain

parts.note: something indisputable is real, beyond doubt

explanation.surface: A claim that some area is undeniably a men-only preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or sphere of activity, a territory someone rules over.

clue.text: They tend to bring up unrelated issues

definitions.text: They tend to bring up unrelated issues

parts.words: They tend to bring up unrelated issues
parts.note: 'bring up' reads as raising topics, and 'issues' as matters, but issues are offspring, raised by carers who are not blood relatives

explanation.surface: A complaint about people who keep raising irrelevant subjects in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Carers who raise children not biologically theirs are the people in this fostering role.

clue.text: She was inclined to get cross with men

definitions.text: She was inclined to get cross with men

parts.words: She was inclined to get cross with men
parts.note: 'get cross with men' suggests losing her temper, but the cross is the X on a ballot paper, which she campaigned to mark as men did

explanation.surface: A woman with a tendency to lose her temper around men.
explanation.definitionFit: Women campaigning for the vote in early twentieth-century Britain wanted to mark ballots on equal terms.

clue.text: With eight members in car, had an accident

indicators.note: accident signals the letters of in car had an are smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A crash involving a car carrying eight people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' suggests passengers or club members; they are limbs. The anagram of IN CAR HAD AN is signalled by 'accident'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders and their relatives have eight legs, and this adjective describes that class.

clue.text: When bow of ship disappears, get to this?

definitions.text: When bow of ship disappears, get to this?

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a vessel, so this picks out the first letter of the word for ship
disappears says that front letter vanishes from the word for ship

parts.note: a craft is a ship or boat

explanation.surface: A grim question about what sailors take to when their vessel goes down bow first.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship is CRAFT; its bow, the front letter C, disappears to leave the answer. Read whole, the clue also describes the makeshift float you scramble onto when a ship sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a simple flat floating platform, the last resort of shipwrecked sailors.

clue.text: Such salesmen may have to deal with knockers

definitions.text: Such salesmen may have to deal with knockers

parts.words: Such salesmen may have to deal with knockers
parts.note: knockers suggests critics or detractors, but these sellers literally handle the knockers on each house's entrance as they call round

explanation.surface: A remark that certain salespeople must put up with critics.
explanation.definitionFit: Salesmen who call at each house in turn sell this way, visiting homes one after another.

clue.text: Once a 12 impeded one, are chores tricky?

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of are chores are twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question whether household jobs are hard, linked to a past militant act.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1913 the suffragette Emily Davison ran onto the Epsom Derby course and brought down the King's horse; 12 is SUFFRAGETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal a suffragette famously obstructed at the Derby was a thoroughbred running in that race.

clue.text: Taking a risk having a beer with a politician

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone chancing it by having a pint with a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' and 'with' are link words; Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory means dependent on chance or luck, like a gamble.

clue.text: It can be hard to negotiate with head — how one may turn cheek?

definitions.text: It can be hard to negotiate with head

parts.note: to 'turn turtle' is to capsize, so turtle is a way one may turn
neck is slang for cheek, meaning impudence or nerve

explanation.surface: Advice about a tricky negotiator and how to turn the other cheek to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiate' suggests bargaining with a boss, but it means getting your head through a tight collar. A boat that capsizes 'turns turtle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A high close-fitting rolled collar on a jumper is famously awkward to pull over your head.

clue.text: Unfinished piece adapted for major work

indicators.note: adapted means the remaining letters are altered into a new order
unfinished means the word piece is left without its final letter

explanation.surface: A fragment left incomplete is reworked into a substantial composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the last letter of PIECE, leaving PIEC, and 'adapted' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long, ambitious poem, film or novel on a grand scale.

clue.text: First of theories supporting flat earth?

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means this letter sits beneath the other piece, holding it up

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface

indicators.note: first of means take only the opening letter of theories

explanation.surface: The first of several ideas behind a belief that the world is flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'earth' is one example of the class, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one example of a world orbiting the Sun.

clue.text: They appear after two stages of descent

definitions.text: They appear after two stages of descent

parts.words: They appear after two stages of descent
parts.note: descent suggests climbing down, but it is family lineage: these relatives come two generations below someone

explanation.surface: Something that shows up after a climber goes down two levels.
explanation.definitionFit: Children of one's children belong to the second generation of descendants.

clue.text: Put out injunction opposing unemployment

definitions.meaning: to extinguish, as with a fire or flame
a command of two words, '...', urging against things being left idle

explanation.surface: A court order against joblessness is extinguished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unemployment' suggests joblessness, but read cryptically it is non-use of something, and the command against it splits the answer as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To douse is to extinguish a fire by drenching it with water.

clue.text: Sucker has to rush off when told

indicators.note: when told means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer's spelling

parts.note: to flee is to rush off or run away

explanation.surface: Someone gullible has to run away once they are informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe, but it is a bloodsucking insect. 'Has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a tiny parasitic insect that feeds by drinking blood.

clue.text: Bishop initially lost in tight game in which draw occurs

indicators.note: initially lost in says the letter for bishop goes missing from the start of the word for tight

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk, as is blotto
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A chess bishop is lost early in a close game that ends in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture makes 'draw' a drawn game; it is the drawing of numbers. B is removed from the start of BLOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style game of chance where numbers are drawn at random.

clue.text: It'll be fine, if the volume's not turned up, and is like this

definitions.text: It'll be fine, if the volume's not turned up, and is like this

parts.words: It'll be fine, if the volume's not turned up, and is like this
parts.note: the surface is about keeping noise down, but a volume is a library book, and a fine is charged when it is not handed back or its loan extended

explanation.surface: Reassurance that all will be well as long as nobody cranks up the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A library loan not extended beyond its due date, which then incurs a penalty charge.

clue.text: Nearly finished the rest in frying-pan

indicators.note: nearly means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to have woke is to have stopped resting, roused from sleep

explanation.surface: Almost done with the leftovers in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished the rest' looks like eating up leftovers; it means stopped resting, WOKE, minus its final E. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wok is a deep round-bottomed pan used for stir-frying in Chinese cooking.

clue.text: Gas supplied clean yet volatile energy

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and changeable, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A description of some fuel that burns clean but is still unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplied' is a link. The surface paints the fuel as clean but unstable, which hides that 'volatile' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylene is a flammable hydrocarbon fuel used in welding torches.

clue.text: Perfunctory gift

definitions.meaning: done only for show or as a minimal gesture, as in a symbolic effort
a voucher given as a present, such as a book voucher

explanation.definitionFit: A gesture made only nominally is this, and a voucher redeemable for goods is also one.
